# Introduction

Today we will get introduced to our final project. You will
read the project description, talk it over with your group, and bring
your questions to the whole class. In the last half hour, you will fill
out the mid-semester survey.

::: callout-note
## The project description

**[Final project: instructions and rubric](https://statistical-history.github.io/project/instructions.html)**
:::


# Part 1: Read (20 minutes)

Read the whole project description on your own.

As you read, write down:

- anything that is **unclear**;
- anything that **surprised** you;
- the **date and contents of the first milestone**;
- **one or two project ideas** that interest you.

# Part 2: Discuss with your group

Sit with your project group. Use these questions to guide the
conversation:

1. What is due at the first milestone? When is it due?
2. Which project ideas interest each of you? Which **two** will your
   group propose, and in what order?
3. What did each of you find unclear? Can the group answer it, or does
   it need to go to the whole class?
4. **How will your group communicate?**

## Before the group discussion ends

- [ ] Your group has a **communication channel** that everyone has
      joined: a group chat, a shared channel, or something similar. Make
      sure every member is in it before you leave the room.
- [ ] Everyone has the others' contact information.
- [ ] You have picked a time to meet before the first milestone is due.
- [ ] If your group would like to use **GitHub** to work together, let
      Kat know.

# Part 3: Whole-class discussion

Bring your group's questions to the whole class. By the end of the
discussion, everyone should be able to answer these questions:

- What is the first milestone, and when is it due?
- What does "everyone contributes to every part" mean in practice?
- What is shared within the group, and what is individual?

## What must be clear before you leave

::: callout-important
## Everyone contributes to every part

Every group member contributes to **every part** of the project:
design, collection, analysis, and checking. Do not divide the project so
that one person only collects data and another person only writes code.
Each person should understand the whole investigation and be able to
explain any part of it.
:::

::: callout-important
## Reports are individual

Each person writes and submits their **own final report**. Your
group may share data, code, tables, and figures, but you write all the
narrative and figure captions yourself. Each report ends with a
**contribution statement** describing the work you did. Keep a
contribution log from the start, so that writing that statement later is
easy.
:::

::: callout-important
## First milestone: Saturday, October 31

**Milestone 1 (two proposed project ideas)** is due **Saturday, October
31, at 11:59 p.m.** Submit one file per group that covers
both ideas. See the project description for what each proposal must
include.
:::

::: callout-tip
## Write down your two projects early

Once your group has chosen its two projects, add them to the
[project sign-up spreadsheet on Canvas](https://canvas.duke.edu/courses/84980/modules/items/1020735) **before you start
writing Milestone 1**. Take a look at what other groups have entered
first. That way you won't find out that another group has already
claimed your project when you are almost done writing.
:::

# Part 4: Mid-semester survey

Use the rest of class to complete the mid-semester survey:

**[Mid-semester survey](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/mWmtnTWeqZ)**

- The survey is **anonymous**. Please be honest. We read every response
  and will use your answers to adjust the rest of the course.
- It **replaces today's exit ticket**, so there is no paper exit ticket
  today.

Once you have submitted the survey, you are free to keep talking with
your group about project ideas.
